top.title: No. 6 Texas women pull away from No. 19 Ohio State
top.description: Breya Cunningham put up a season-high 24 points and 13 rebounds to help No. 6 Texas defeat No. 19 Ohio State 75-61 on Nov. 22 in Fort Worth, Texas. Jayda Clark tallied 15 points, seven rebounds and five assists for the Longhorns (6-0), while Texas star Madison Booker scored all 12 of her points in the second half after shooting 0 for 5 and committing five turnovers before halftime. Texas shot 35.8% overall and 2 for 11 from 3-point range but hit 25 of 26 free throws (96.2%). Cunningham and Booker each went 6 for 6 from the line, as Texas won every quarter and scored the first 16 points of the fourth quarter to blow open a reasonably close game. Jaloni Cambridge scored 27 points for Ohio State (5-2), and Ava Watson and Sydney Mobley added 8 each. The Buckeyes scored 29 points off 20 Texas turnovers to stay in striking distance until the fourth quarter. They fell behind 75-48 before scoring the final 13 points of the game. Texas won the battle on the boards 49-33 and scored 21 second-chance points off 20 offensive rebounds. top.title: Victor Wembanyama's latest 50-point game came with an ethical dilemma
top.description: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) takes a 3-point shot during the second quarter of an NBA game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. The Spurs won 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) With 6:27 remaining Saturday and the Spurs ahead by 23 points, Victor Wembanyama rose for a step-back 3-pointer from the right arc. From his post on the sidelines, Spurs coach Mitch Johnson looked on with pit in his stomach, as if his job depended on the shot going in. Which, perhaps, it did. "I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did," Johnson said. With one final swish, Wembanyama gave Johnson his wish. The shot pushed Wembanyama to an even 50 points, putting the finishing touch on another game for the ages by the All-Star center in a 114-91 blowout victory over the Pelicans. It also allowed Johnson to get his franchise player off the floor and to the safety of the Spurs' bench without an argument. "It would have been hard to take him out that close to 50," Johnson said. Not for the first time this season, Wembanyama's final stat line Saturday looked like something that fell out of Wilt Chamberlain's Basketball Reference page: 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals. Wembanyama didn't arrive at the Frost Bank Center with any grand designs on producing a box score never before recorded in NBA history. It just sort of happened that way. "They just come when we play the right way as a team," the 7-foot-4 Frenchman said. "I just want to stack them up. Hopefully there is many more coming." Before Saturday, no player in the NBA this season had put up a game of at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals. Wembanyama had that by halftime. His night began with a 17-point first quarter, a career high. He ended it with the third 50-point game of his career. Perhaps the most eye-popping part of Wembanyama's latest eruption was that it wasn't even his best performance of the season. That distinction belongs to his 52-point, 24-rebound, eight-block opus in a Nov. 4 victory over Dallas. "Sometimes you can feel a special game brewing," Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox said. "That first quarter you could definitely feel it coming. We try to make some of his baskets easier, and when he does those special things you feel those special things." Thanks to his most recent outburst, Wembanyama will head into Monday's game at Sacramento averaging 29.9 points per game, third-most in the league behind the Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic and Oklahoma City's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Propelled by Wembanyama, the Spurs won for the 14 th time in 15 games, improving their season record to 14-3 to equal the Lakers and Philadelphia 76ers for the best in the league. top.title: Well, That’s Better: Marquette 106, Chicago State 62
top.description: Michael Phillips had himself a nice outing against the Cougars. | Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images When Colin Porter missed a three-pointer with 14:10 left to go in the first half, that went into the scorebooks as Marquette’s first missed field goal of the game. Yes, nearly six straight minutes without missing a shot. Your score at the time: Marquette 22, Chicago State 10. The Golden Eagles had just answered a 5-0 CSU burst with nine straight before the Cougars cashed in a three-pointer to break up that run. For the next few minutes, it was actually a back and forth basketball game. From the 12 minute mark of the first half until there was under eight minutes left, neither team scored two buckets in a row. That left Marquette up just 12 points even though they had led by as many as 17 at one point. And then Marquette discovered the EVAPORATE button. 10 straight for the Golden Eagles, with Royce Parham hitting two three-pointers along the way. Then a free throw from CSU’s Mike Price, then a three from Michael Phillips, then a layup from CSU’s Foday Sheriff, then another 10 straight points from Marquette to end the half. 10-0 run to end the half, or 13-2 if you prefer, or 23-3 if you prefer. Marquette by 32, 57-25, at intermission. The lead hit 40 for the first time on a triple from Phillips as part of a 9-0 run in the second half as MU blew the margin out to 75-31 with 15:03 to play. That 44 point gap would be the largest lead of the game for Marquette as Chicago State did managed to shave some space off of that, first with an immediate 8-0 run, and back-to-back three-pointers from Davius Loury got the Cougars as close as 34. That’s the most that Marquette allowed, and then they closed the game on an 18-8 run. Never more than five at a time, but that’s how they ended up back at 44 to end it. For historic purposes: Ian Miletic got Marquette over the century mark with a three-pointer with 1:38 to go, and that shot tied the program record for threes by a team in a game. Miletic then broke that record with Marquette’s 19th three-pointer of the game with 54 seconds left. That's a NEW SCHOOL RECORD for three pointers made with 19!!🔥🔥 @Ian7Miletic with his third triple in the second half. #MUBB | #WeAreMarquette pic.twitter.com/evo166QA4i — Marquette Men’s Basketball (@MarquetteMBB) November 22, 2026 Your leading scorer here was Adrien Stevens, who put up 18 points on 6-for-11 shooting, with four of his five misses coming as part of his 5-for-9 three-point shooting on the day. Royce Parham had 16, Sananda Fru and Michael Phillips both had 13, and Nigel James added 11. Nolan Minessale’s five rebounds led the Golden Eagles in that column, and James had seven assists in 20 foul-and-margin shortened minutes. In case you were wondering: Marquette shot 75% on two-pointers here, which is a marked improvement on what they’ve looked like in general this season. They also grabbed 67% of their rare misses and limited Chicago State to just 39% of their misses

top.title: ‘Massive loser’: DK Metcalf’s nightmare season continues with ejection
top.description: Oct 12, 2025; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf (4) makes a catch for a touchdown during the fourth quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images DK Metcalf was already having a disastrous 2026 season coming into Sunday, and the Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver didn’t do anything this afternoon to help his cause. Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of today’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles after earning his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The two-time Pro Bowler got into it with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean and a few of his teammates during his final confrontation, finishing the day with one reception for two yards, two personal fouls and one ejecction. Acquired before the 2025 season in a trade with the Seattle Seahawks, Metcalf has not lived up to the lucrative contract extension Pittsburgh gave him. In 10 games this fall, he’s recorded only 35 receptions for 432 yards and two touchdowns. ‘ Hard to find someone having a worse season’ Metcalf’s ejection elicited plenty of online reaction, including from some fed-up Steelers fans. “ There has never been a bigger loser to play for the Steelers than DK Metcalf . Just a gigantic, massive loser,” said Pittsburgh-based sportswriter Adam Gretz . “ Hard to find someone having a worse season than DK Metcalf . Guy is absolutely sabotaging his own offense. Steelers just got better by him getting ejected,” added NFL writer Sam Monson . “ Trading DK Metcalf when he did was one of John Schneider’s greatest moves as #Seahawks GM,” said BBC Sheffield’s Rob Staton . “ DK Metcalf and Aaron Rodgers are the worst QB-WR marriage in the league,” chimed in Yahoo Sports’ Josh Norris. “ The Steelers traded away a “problem” WR to go out and trade for DK Metcalf, w ho costed them a 2nd, $132M extension, is much worse than George Pickens + is even more of a problem WR. Hilarious franchise decision making,” said Matt of Six Rings of Steel . More punishment incoming? Today was the third ejection of Metcalf’s career, and KOA Colorado’s Benjamin Allbright tweeted moments ago that it could cost him his next game as well. “ League source suggests that DK Metcalf could be seeing an additional suspension and miss the Broncos game on Friday,” Allbright said . “ Metcalf has been ejected in two previous games and is considered a repeat offender.” The Steelers are scheduled to take on the Broncos at 3 p.m. ET on Black Friday. top.title: Liverpool vs Man United player ratings: Two 9/10s inspire as Mauricio Pochettino endures nightmare bow
top.description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a dismal start to his tenure at Manchester United as Liverpool ran riot in a 4-0 victory against their relegation-threatened rivals. A whirlwind week for the former Argentina international ended in familiar disappointment for the struggling visitors, whose hopes of a new manager bounce were decisively crushed during a nightmare opening 13 minutes at Anfield. Dominik Szoboszlai put the hosts ahead with a fierce free-kick after defender Leny Yoro was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity inside just eight minutes, before Florian Wirtz ’s smart finish quickly put Pochettino’s side further behind. United managed to temporarily stem the tide courtesy of crucial Senne Lammens saves, last-ditch defending, and wayward finishing, but Andoni Iraola’s side redoubled their efforts after the interval. Pochettino’s 10 men were frankly fortunate that Liverpool only added two more goals through Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz, such was the overwhelming nature of their dominance. Here are how the players rated at Anfield: Liverpool Alisson - 7 Smart stop to deny Fernandes when Man United started knocking at the door in the first half, alive to the situation after not being required in the early stages. Barely got a touch after the break, until being called until action in stoppage time to deny Fernandes consolation. Ronald Araujo - 8 His through ball for Isak was more of a hooked clearance than a calculated lofted pass, but it still caused the chaos required to get Yoro sent off. Always willing to get in the challenge. Subbed. top.description: In past regular seasons, the Boston Celtics have generally churned out win after win, especially under head coach Joe Mazzulla. However, after resting multiple key players against the struggling Sacramento Kings on Saturday night and falling to them, 97-96, the C's are at risk of losing four games in a row. That'd be enough for Boston's longest losing streak since the 2020-21 season, which was back when de facto Celtics general manager Brad Stevens was still the head coach of the Green Team. Such a skid can be avoided if the 11-5 Celtics are able to topple the 8-8 Golden State Warriors on Sunday evening in San Francisco. The C's may be tired because they're playing on the second night of a back-to-back — their fourth time doing so this November — but attempting to bounce back from arguably their worst defeat of the season could serve as motivation. Although, one could say the same about the Warriors, who are currently on a five-game losing streak (the longest active slide in the Western Conference) that's coincided with the injury absence of star point guard Stephen Curry. The future Hall of Famer won't return versus the Celtics, but star forward Jayson Tatum could take the floor again for Boston after resting on Saturday. No matter who plays, the C's should expect a tough battle from a rested Warriors squad in one of the loudest arenas in the NBA. The Dubs have lost five straight games and hold a .500 record (8-8). For the moment, they sit just outside of Play-In territory with the eleventh seed in the West. top.title: Carlos Alcaraz adds ATP Finals title to glittering trophy cabinet
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Spanish tennis player Carlos Alcaraz celebrates defeating US' Ben Shelton during their men's singles semifinal match of the 2026 Nitto ATP Finals, an international tennis match in Turin. (is associated with: «Carlos Alcaraz adds ATP Finals title to glittering trophy cabinet») Mickael Chavet/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa Carlos Alcaraz made more history with a maiden ATP Finals title after a straight-sets win over Alexander Zverev. A 6-2 7-6 (7) triumph in Turin enabled seven-time major champion Alcaraz to follow in the footsteps of Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic by becoming the fourth male player to win the end-of-season tournament along with each four grand slams in their career. Alcaraz had finished runner-up to Jannik Sinner in 2025 and lost twice to current world number one Zverev previously in the competition, but showed why many still proclaim the Spaniard to be the best player in the world after an impressive two-hour-and-two-minutes victory. With strapping on his left leg and after a gruelling three-set battle with Ben Shelton on Saturday, Alcaraz set about becoming the first player of the week to take a set off French Open and US Open champion Zverev. Top seed Zverev was forced to dig deep to hold on his first service game, but was broken three times during a one-sided opening set. Alcaraz broke again to move 2-1 up in the second before a 4-2 lead was established. However, Alcaraz let slip his advantage and a topsy-turvy tie-break followed between the first and second seed. After Alcaraz claimed an early break, Zverev reeled off six points in a row, but failed to take three set points. Then at the second time of asking, after one match point was saved, Alcaraz produced a bullet backhand to defeat Zverev and he duly collapsed to the ground after winning the 30th title of his extraordinary career and sixth of an injury-hit 2026. "This trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me," Alcaraz said on-court. "Today's final, I needed to put the three c's that my grandpa always tells me that I have to give every time that I step on the court for every match and every practice. "He's watching at home, so I just want to say I love you to my grandparents. In Spanish it's 'Cabeza, corazon, cajones', in English it is 'head, heart, balls', so I think today that was about it."

top.title: I feel the pain: Pochettino takes responsibility for Man Utd hammering
top.description: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Manchester United at the Anfield. (is associated with: «I feel the pain: Pochettino takes responsibility for Man Utd hammering») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Mauricio Pochettino accepted full responsibility for the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool as he endured the worst debut by a Manchester United manager in 100 years. Not since player-manager Lal Hilditch lost 4-0 to Bolton in October 1926 had a new boss endured such a chastening start, which left the club 19th in the Premier League, two points away from climbing out of the bottom three. But while the head coach said he took full ownership of the result, he felt the eighth-minute red card shown to Leny Yoro changed the course of the game. The defender's dismissal for denying Alexander Isak a goalscoring opportunity following Matthijs de Ligt's mistake allowed Dominik Szoboszlai to score from the resulting free-kick. A brilliant twisting volley from Florian Wirtz, his fifth goal in four games for club and country, doubled the lead and while Liverpool should have added plenty more, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz compounded a chastening evening for Pochettino in the second half. It proved too much for some fans in the visiting section with police called to deal with a disturbance with one man being led away in handcuffs. "It is painful because it is 4-0 but we play more than 80 minutes with 10 men. I take responsibility for that, no worries," said Pochettino, who argued a challenge by Jeremy Jacquet on Bryan Mbeumo before the red card should have resulted in a penalty. "We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is true. "You need to look at the circumstance because it is so easy to talk so cheap. We lose one game; we are not going to lose more than one game how we lose today. "We have a lot of work to do and we take responsibility. We feel the pain but the thing is to keep working." United have conceded 23 goals in 11 league matches and Pochettino's decision to hand De Ligt his first Premier League start in a year drew scrutiny, which only increased with the defender's performance. "The team concede because the balance is not so good and I take responsibility for that," said the Argentinian. "He (De Ligt) was training, he played in the Champions League before the international duty and when we arrived we saw the combinations." Asked whether he had inherited a relegation battle, Pochettino added: "Still a lot of games to play. We need to accept the reality and we need to be united and all together. "We feel disappointed because it is clear after what happened (Yoro's red card) happened the plan was in the bin. "What I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they are committed to the team, to the club and they want to win games. "Today we made an effort. Today was a test that, for me, is very positive." Victory was only Liverpool's second at home

top.title: Leeds United Have Strong Chance Of Striking This Striker Bargain: Should Farke Push For Him?
top.description: Leeds United Have Strong Chance Of Striking This Striker Bargain: Should Farke Push For Him? Leeds United have a strong chance of signing Stuttgart striker Ermedin Demirović, according to Sport Witness , which cites Tuttosport. Leeds pursued the 28-year-old over the summer, and the report says his own eagerness to leave now gives them an edge. Demirović has agreed to no new contract and his current deal expires in 2028, so Tuttosport expect his summer valuation of €30m (roughly £26m) to fall sharply. Milan are the main obstacle. The report says their incoming sporting director, Markus Krösche, knows the Bosnian forward well, and other Premier League clubs are interested. He arrives in good form. Tuttosport credits him with nine goals in 15 appearances in the Bundesliga and Champions League this season, and FotMob ‘s data supports the finishing, with 4.76 expected goals from nine league games. His limits are clear. He wins only 25.6% of his aerial duels and ranks low for touches and chances created, so he finishes moves rather than starting them. That profile matters because of how Daniel Farke sets Leeds up. His 3-5-2 needs two forwards, yet Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who scored 14 Premier League goals last season, has battled foot trouble since the 1-1 draw with Manchester United in October. Leeds now sit sixth after the demolition of Chelsea, but they scored once or not at all in each of their last six league games leading up to this. Should Leeds United push for Demirović in January? STUTTGART, GERMANY – OCTOBER 23: Ermedin Demirovic of VfB Stuttgart celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between VfB Stuttgart and Borussia Mönchengladbach at MHPArena on October 23, 2026 in Stuttgart, Germany. (Photo by Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Getty Images) Yes, but only at the right price and for a specific job. Leeds don’t need a replacement for Calvert-Lewin, whose box movement and aerial threat drive Farke’s crossing game through Jayden Bogle and James Justin. They need a second striker who finishes chances. Calvert-Lewin wasted several against Spurs, and Demirović’s expected goals suggest he reaches good positions and takes them. His defensive numbers suggest he would press from the front without breaking the 3-5-2’s shape. The risk is the delivery. A forward who loses three aerial duels in four makes a poor target for wing-back crosses, so Farke would need him running beyond Calvert-Lewin rather than competing with him. FotMob values him at €17m (about £15m), and the summer’s £26m now looks excessive for a 28-year-old. Krösche’s knowledge of him gives Milan an advantage, so Leeds can’t assume his eagerness to leave guarantees a move to Elland Road. If Stuttgart hold out, Leeds should spend on a different attacker. At around £15m he fixes a finishing problem; at £26m he becomes a risk.

nigeria.title: Tinubu Urges APC Leaders To Unite Ahead Of 2027 Elections
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has called on leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to reconcile their differences ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscoring the virtue of forgiveness. He made the call on Sunday at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family in Lagos State, urging APC leaders to forgive one another and seek reconciliation. His message was specifically directed at his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Ibrahim Masari, and former defence minister, Abubakar Badaru, both of whom were in the audience at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club, where the President spoke. ﻿ While reacting to reports of a misunderstanding between Governor Dikko Radda and Masari in Katsina State, Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, urged Masari to go back home to reconcile with his governor. “Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the President’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile with them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” the President said. He also gave the same order to Badaru, the former governor of Jigawa State. President Tinubu appealed to all APC leaders to set aside personal differences, strengthen internal cohesion, and work collectively to consolidate his administration’s gains ahead of the 2027 elections. He thanked the organisers of the Islamic prayer session and clerics who prayed for him, his administration, and Nigeria. ‘Obstacles Were On Our Way’ He also thanked God for his victory in the 2023 presidential election, despite formidable obstacles which he said “were on our way”. “People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no ₦5 in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel. “We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said. The President recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022. “It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible,” he was quoted as saying. He appealed to Lagosians to come out en masse on Election Day to exercise their right to vote. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” the President said. “We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he emphasised. He reaffirmed his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for all Nigerians. nigeria.description: …Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law books By Innocent Anaba LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resources that will enrich Nigerian jurisprudence and strengthen the intellectual foundation of the legal profession. Kekere-Ekun, who spoke, weekend, while chairing the public presentation of the books in Lagos, said the publications reflected an impressive combination of legal scholarship, practical experience and engagement with contemporary developments in the administration of justice. She noted that the collection, comprising four books authored by Pinheiro and two compilations produced in his honour, addressed significant areas of legal practice, including litigation, arbitration, insolvency, criminal law, technology and contemporary jurisprudence. According to her, the publications were not merely a collection of books assembled to commemorate an accomplished legal practitioner but works that sought to make legal knowledge more accessible and useful to those responsible for applying, interpreting and developing the law. The CJN said: “Taken together, the works reflect an engagement with important areas of legal practice and scholarship, as well as an attempt to preserve the experiences and contributions of a distinguished member of our profession.” Kekere-Ekun described ‘Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk’ as particularly significant because it offered a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar. She observed that memoirs of this nature were valuable because they preserved aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records. Such accounts, she said, enabled younger practitioners to appreciate the human experiences behind professional milestones, including the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompanied a successful legal career. The CJN also highlighted the importance of the two publications on arbitration and insolvency, particularly against the background of Nigeria’s increasingly sophisticated business environment and the need for effective legal responses to commercial transactions. , financial distress and dispute resolution. Similarly, she described Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure as an important contribution to an increasingly relevant area of law under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. According to her, its examination of corporate rescue, restructuring, administration and other mechanisms for addressing financial distress reflected the growing recognition that preserving viable businesses could, in appropriate circumstances, better serve creditors, employees, investors and the wider economy than immediate liquidation.

nigeria.title: 2027: Any party saying I’ve stepped down is working for Tinubu - Atiku
nigeria.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused political parties spreading claims that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race of working in favour of President Bola Tinubu. Atiku described the reports as false and insisted that he remained in the contest to win the election. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice-president said no group claiming to be his supporters had the authority to announce his withdrawal. “Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field,” he said. Atiku added that he had not made any decision to leave the race, dismissing claims attributed to individuals presenting themselves as his supporters. “Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision,” he said. He warned that any attempt to remove him from the contest through fabricated declarations would deny Nigerians the opportunity to choose their preferred candidate. “If I am not on the ballot, Bola Tinubu might as well wait for a coronation. But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice,” he said. The former vice-president also accused those behind the reports of using misinformation to weaken the opposition, alleging that the tactic was intended to benefit the ruling All Progressives Congress. He urged opposition parties seeking to defeat Tinubu to focus on persuading voters rather than circulating claims about rival candidates. “Anyone serious about defeating the APC should take their case to voters. Manufacturing supporters and circulating false declarations will not defeat Tinubu. It only serves him,” Atiku said. On his campaign activities, Atiku said his Affordable Life agenda remained focused on addressing the economic difficulties confronting Nigerian households. He cited the rising cost of food and transportation as issues his campaign intended to address, saying the campaign was reaching communities across the country. “Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport,” he said. Atiku urged his supporters to remain mobilised ahead of the election and ensure they had their Permanent Voter Cards. He reiterated that he would not withdraw in favour of any other candidate, declaring that the contest would be decided by voters. “I do not need anyone to step down for me, and I am stepping down for no one,” he said. The statement concluded with Atiku expressing confidence that he would defeat Tinubu at the ballot box on January 16, 2027. nigeria.title: Horror in Calabar: Driver runs over Nursing student twice, flees
nigeria.description: By Emma Una CALABAR—A nursing student of the School of Nursing, Mary Slessor Avenue, Calabar, identified as Cynthia Eni, has been killed after a speeding driver reportedly knocked her down and reversed to run over her a second time before fleeing the scene. The incident, which occurred at the weekend, happened as Cynthia was crossing the road into the school compound after going out with two colleagues to buy some items. A friend of the deceased, Mercy, who witnessed the incident, said the driver first knocked Cynthia down before reversing and running over her again as people attempted to come to her rescue. “It was a bewildering scene. When the car knocked her down, we were shouting for help and before some boys could rush down, the same car returned and climbed her again. When the car was approaching we thought the driver had come to help but was surprised when the car ran over her again.” Mercy said the driver took advantage of the fading light and the fact that people were focused on the victim to escape, adding that the vehicle’s registration number was not visible. She said Cynthia, who was about 30, had completed her Community Health studies at the College of Health Technology and enrolled at the School of Nursing to obtain an additional qualification. “We don’t know what was in the driver’s mind. Even if he was drunk or had some issues with Cynthia, he should have had some sense of humanity and not come back to crush her the way he did.” Mercy said she could not recall any misunderstanding between the deceased and fellow students or outsiders. “We leave everything to God,” she said, breaking down in tears. There was no official at the Provost’s Office available to comment on the incident as it occurred at the weekend. entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. entertainment.title: Tochukwu Ekoh: What My Friend’s Passing Taught Me About Kindness
entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? What was the reason for that reconnection, and why did it have to end this way? The timing of certain events leaves you with more questions than answers. What makes this loss even more difficult to comprehend is how it happened. I had been the one who suffered an accident, yet I survived and was gradually recovering. He wasn’t sick. sports.title: Victor Wembanyama's latest 50-point game came with an ethical dilemma
sports.description: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) takes a 3-point shot during the second quarter of an NBA game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. The Spurs won 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) With 6:27 remaining Saturday and the Spurs ahead by 23 points, Victor Wembanyama rose for a step-back 3-pointer from the right arc. From his post on the sidelines, Spurs coach Mitch Johnson looked on with pit in his stomach, as if his job depended on the shot going in. Which, perhaps, it did. "I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did," Johnson said. With one final swish, Wembanyama gave Johnson his wish. The shot pushed Wembanyama to an even 50 points, putting the finishing touch on another game for the ages by the All-Star center in a 114-91 blowout victory over the Pelicans. It also allowed Johnson to get his franchise player off the floor and to the safety of the Spurs' bench without an argument. "It would have been hard to take him out that close to 50," Johnson said. Not for the first time this season, Wembanyama's final stat line Saturday looked like something that fell out of Wilt Chamberlain's Basketball Reference page: 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals. Wembanyama didn't arrive at the Frost Bank Center with any grand designs on producing a box score never before recorded in NBA history. It just sort of happened that way. "They just come when we play the right way as a team," the 7-foot-4 Frenchman said. "I just want to stack them up. Hopefully there is many more coming." Before Saturday, no player in the NBA this season had put up a game of at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals. Wembanyama had that by halftime. His night began with a 17-point first quarter, a career high. He ended it with the third 50-point game of his career. Perhaps the most eye-popping part of Wembanyama's latest eruption was that it wasn't even his best performance of the season. That distinction belongs to his 52-point, 24-rebound, eight-block opus in a Nov. 4 victory over Dallas. "Sometimes you can feel a special game brewing," Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox said. "That first quarter you could definitely feel it coming. We try to make some of his baskets easier, and when he does those special things you feel those special things." Thanks to his most recent outburst, Wembanyama will head into Monday's game at Sacramento averaging 29.9 points per game, third-most in the league behind the Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic and Oklahoma City's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Propelled by Wembanyama, the Spurs won for the 14 th time in 15 games, improving their season record to 14-3 to equal the Lakers and Philadelphia 76ers for the best in the league. sports.description: FILE PHOTO - Spanish tennis player Carlos Alcaraz celebrates defeating US' Ben Shelton during their men's singles semifinal match of the 2026 Nitto ATP Finals, an international tennis match in Turin. (is associated with: «Carlos Alcaraz adds ATP Finals title to glittering trophy cabinet») Mickael Chavet/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa Carlos Alcaraz made more history with a maiden ATP Finals title after a straight-sets win over Alexander Zverev. A 6-2 7-6 (7) triumph in Turin enabled seven-time major champion Alcaraz to follow in the footsteps of Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic by becoming the fourth male player to win the end-of-season tournament along with each four grand slams in their career. Alcaraz had finished runner-up to Jannik Sinner in 2025 and lost twice to current world number one Zverev previously in the competition, but showed why many still proclaim the Spaniard to be the best player in the world after an impressive two-hour-and-two-minutes victory. With strapping on his left leg and after a gruelling three-set battle with Ben Shelton on Saturday, Alcaraz set about becoming the first player of the week to take a set off French Open and US Open champion Zverev. Top seed Zverev was forced to dig deep to hold on his first service game, but was broken three times during a one-sided opening set. Alcaraz broke again to move 2-1 up in the second before a 4-2 lead was established. However, Alcaraz let slip his advantage and a topsy-turvy tie-break followed between the first and second seed. After Alcaraz claimed an early break, Zverev reeled off six points in a row, but failed to take three set points. Then at the second time of asking, after one match point was saved, Alcaraz produced a bullet backhand to defeat Zverev and he duly collapsed to the ground after winning the 30th title of his extraordinary career and sixth of an injury-hit 2026. "This trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me," Alcaraz said on-court. "Today's final, I needed to put the three c's that my grandpa always tells me that I have to give every time that I step on the court for every match and every practice. "He's watching at home, so I just want to say I love you to my grandparents. In Spanish it's 'Cabeza, corazon, cajones', in English it is 'head, heart, balls', so I think today that was about it."

sports.title: I feel the pain: Pochettino takes responsibility for Man Utd hammering

Not since player-manager Lal Hilditch lost 4-0 to Bolton in October 1926 had a new boss endured such a chastening start, which left the club 19th in the Premier League, two points away from climbing out of the bottom three. But while the head coach said he took full ownership of the result, he felt the eighth-minute red card shown to Leny Yoro changed the course of the game. The defender's dismissal for denying Alexander Isak a goalscoring opportunity following Matthijs de Ligt's mistake allowed Dominik Szoboszlai to score from the resulting free-kick. A brilliant twisting volley from Florian Wirtz, his fifth goal in four games for club and country, doubled the lead and while Liverpool should have added plenty more, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz compounded a chastening evening for Pochettino in the second half. It proved too much for some fans in the visiting section with police called to deal with a disturbance with one man being led away in handcuffs. "It is painful because it is 4-0 but we play more than 80 minutes with 10 men. I take responsibility for that, no worries," said Pochettino, who argued a challenge by Jeremy Jacquet on Bryan Mbeumo before the red card should have resulted in a penalty. "We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is true. "You need to look at the circumstance because it is so easy to talk so cheap. We lose one game; we are not going to lose more than one game how we lose today. "We have a lot of work to do and we take responsibility. We feel the pain but the thing is to keep working." United have conceded 23 goals in 11 league matches and Pochettino's decision to hand De Ligt his first Premier League start in a year drew scrutiny, which only increased with the defender's performance. "The team concede because the balance is not so good and I take responsibility for that," said the Argentinian. "He (De Ligt) was training, he played in the Champions League before the international duty and when we arrived we saw the combinations." Asked whether he had inherited a relegation battle, Pochettino added: "Still a lot of games to play. We need to accept the reality and we need to be united and all together. "We feel disappointed because it is clear after what happened (Yoro's red card) happened the plan was in the bin. "What I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they are committed to the team, to the club and they want to win games. "Today we made an effort. Today was a test that, for me, is very positive." Victory was only Liverpool's second at home

sports.title: Leeds United Have Strong Chance Of Striking This Striker Bargain: Should Farke Push For Him?
sports.description: Leeds United Have Strong Chance Of Striking This Striker Bargain: Should Farke Push For Him? Leeds United have a strong chance of signing Stuttgart striker Ermedin Demirović, according to Sport Witness , which cites Tuttosport. Leeds pursued the 28-year-old over the summer, and the report says his own eagerness to leave now gives them an edge. Demirović has agreed to no new contract and his current deal expires in 2028, so Tuttosport expect his summer valuation of €30m (roughly £26m) to fall sharply. Milan are the main obstacle. The report says their incoming sporting director, Markus Krösche, knows the Bosnian forward well, and other Premier League clubs are interested. He arrives in good form. Tuttosport credits him with nine goals in 15 appearances in the Bundesliga and Champions League this season, and FotMob ‘s data supports the finishing, with 4.76 expected goals from nine league games. His limits are clear. He wins only 25.6% of his aerial duels and ranks low for touches and chances created, so he finishes moves rather than starting them. That profile matters because of how Daniel Farke sets Leeds up. His 3-5-2 needs two forwards, yet Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who scored 14 Premier League goals last season, has battled foot trouble since the 1-1 draw with Manchester United in October. Leeds now sit sixth after the demolition of Chelsea, but they scored once or not at all in each of their last six league games leading up to this. Should Leeds United push for Demirović in January? STUTTGART, GERMANY – OCTOBER 23: Ermedin Demirovic of VfB Stuttgart celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between VfB Stuttgart and Borussia Mönchengladbach at MHPArena on October 23, 2026 in Stuttgart, Germany. (Photo by Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Getty Images) Yes, but only at the right price and for a specific job. Leeds don’t need a replacement for Calvert-Lewin, whose box movement and aerial threat drive Farke’s crossing game through Jayden Bogle and James Justin. They need a second striker who finishes chances. Calvert-Lewin wasted several against Spurs, and Demirović’s expected goals suggest he reaches good positions and takes them. His defensive numbers suggest he would press from the front without breaking the 3-5-2’s shape. The risk is the delivery. A forward who loses three aerial duels in four makes a poor target for wing-back crosses, so Farke would need him running beyond Calvert-Lewin rather than competing with him. FotMob values him at €17m (about £15m), and the summer’s £26m now looks excessive for a 28-year-old. Krösche’s knowledge of him gives Milan an advantage, so Leeds can’t assume his eagerness to leave guarantees a move to Elland Road. If Stuttgart hold out, Leeds should spend on a different attacker. At around £15m he fixes a finishing problem; at £26m he becomes a risk.

technology.title: As cars go digital, US consumers pay an extra $12 billion a year for repairs
technology.description: The computerization of cars comes at a price to US consumers, according to the Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), which says that software fees and other charges faced by mechanics push up garage costs. An investigation by the non-profit consumer group estimates that car repair costs for Americans have been inflated by $12 billion each year, as vehicles integrate more computerized functions. Its report, Closing Shop , is available online. To find a failed sensor, release an electronic parking brake, or perform diagnostics, a technician has to first connect a laptop or tablet to the vehicle. To so this, the repair shop has to have the right software tools, and that means paying the vehicle manufacturer subscription charges and other fees, in order to get the information they need to complete the job. If smaller independent repair shops can’t afford all the necessary software or subscriptions, they may be forced to steer customers to authorized dealerships for some fixes – about one in five jobs – and this allows the latter to charge more. PIRG claims that drivers pay for this through their insurance premiums, even if they never need to get their car fixed, because higher repair costs mean higher insurance claims. It says the price of auto insurance has risen three times as fast as the rest of the US economy since 2012. Even if mechanics do choose to pay for the software, they spend an estimated collective 83 million hours a year buying, downloading, logging in, and waiting. At typical repair rates, that adds up to $12 billion. A separate report from the PIRG Education Fund claims that a two-tiered repair model now exists, where independent sites conduct repairs with less information, less powerful diagnostic tools, and higher associated costs than the authorized dealerships. The advocacy group wants to see legislators take this issue in hand, and has a number of recommendations for them. One is to stop manufacturers from locking out independent mechanics from simple repair jobs like changing brake pads, and require them to support a standard protocol for authenticating independent diagnostic tools. Another is to give owners control over their vehicle’s data via a standardized platform for accessing telematics repair information, so that the owner can give access to an independent repair shop. Car firms can use the vehicle data to tell owners that a repair is needed and to take it to an approved repair shop, without even disclosing what the issue is. DIY repairers should be able to get everything they need to fix their own cars. Service information and basic diagnostic software should be free, and PIRG also wants a cap on the license fees manufacturers charge for their official software tools. “We’ve allowed car manufacturers to build a toll road between the mechanic and the repair,” says Nathan Proctor, leader of PIRG’s Right to Repair campaign and co-author on the report. “We have a plethora of tolls on the road – subscriptions you need for m

science.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
science.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

science.title: SpaceX sends classified US spy satellites to orbit in early-morning launch from California coast (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the NROL-136 mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office from California on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the U.S. Space Force , and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 is the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

science.title: This viral star projector has been hyped to Mars and back, but we hunted down the best version you can buy
science.description: It was only a matter of time, but AI has come for astronomy accessories. I’ve yet to see a fictional elderly craftsman begging you to buy his hand-carved telescopes; however, it has absolutely muddied the waters around this viral gooseneck Galaxy Projector Night Light. The good news is that there is an impressive little star projector to be had here, and I’m here to cut through the AI-assisted hype. To make sure you’re not hoodwinked, I’ve done the online legwork to bring you the best version of this device, and it won’t cost you a fortune to put a planetarium in your pocket. Before we dive into what makes this Galaxy Projector Night Light so great, there are a couple of pressing issues to address. No variant of this USB-powered star projector will break up heated dinner arguments by casting a beautifully animated space whale on the ceiling, as one ridiculous AI-generated advert asserts. Its projections are eye-catching enough to entertain space fans young and old, but they’re strictly static. Also, while you might be tempted by the lure of 24 interchangeable slides, compared to this Galaxy Projector Night Light’s 13, this lesser model’s slide selection is a letdown. Not only are the slides smaller and blurrier than this model, a large number are dedicated to seasonal holidays. As much as I enjoy Christmas, if I had Santa’s colossal face gazing down at me from the ceiling I’d never sleep again. Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light review More than meets the eye Aside from the projector itself, the Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light includes 13 swappable slides, crammed into a compact box. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) I tempered my expectations when I first got my hands on the Galaxy Projector Night Light. Packed in a small, relatively unassuming box, it looks remarkably similar to the standard model that’s spread across TikTok, YouTube, Facebook and so on. Just like that one, it’s powered via USB, with a flexible stalk, a slot for slides and a nose-mounted focus wheel. However, once I hooked it up to a handy USB socket, all my reservations vanished, and I was seriously impressed by the power of this little projector. You’ll need a darkened room but the Galaxy Projector Night Light’s larger lens is a serious step-up from the run-of-the-mill version. Its images are richer and clearer than you’d expect from a projector this size, and easily capable of transforming a mid-sized ceiling or wall into a cosmic display. This stunning image of the Pillars of Creation originally came from the James Webb Space Telescope. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) This stunning James Webb Space Telescope image of the Pillars of Creation, with its vast columns of gas and dust, is a perfect example of the projections on offer. The fact the display was static didn’t diminish its wow factor, and I spent a good 15 minutes gazing at it in wonder. The Galaxy Projector Night Light does have a four-hour shut-off in case you drift off or want to use it

science.title: As 'Star Trek: First Contact' turns 30, Director Jonathan Frakes reflects on his triumphant time-travel blockbuster (interview)
science.description: null " Star Trek: First Contact " celebrates its 30th anniversary today, and the engaging sci-fi classic still looks fantastic three decades later. With the sad passing of its star, Patrick Stewart , last month, and "Star Trek's" milestone 60th birthday taking place in 2026, this is a bittersweet salute that also holds an extra special significance. Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes , in his feature film debut, " First Contact " consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved. Based on a compelling screenplay by Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore, "First Contact" remains as bright and beautiful as ever, brimming with bravado, heart, horror, and heroism. Not only was it a bona fide crowdpleaser when it was released by Paramount over Thanksgiving week on Nov. 22, 1996, but it was also a financial success for the studio, eventually pulling in a worldwide total of $212 million off a modest $45 million budget. Honestly, who can forget Alice Krige's seductive Borg Queen, Marina Sirtis’ Deana Troi tipsy on tequila, Brent Spiner's Data feeling the sensation of human skin, Patrick Stewart’s Jean-Luc Picard reliving past traumas, and James Cromwell's Zephram Cochrane blasting off in the Phoenix and dancing to Roy Orbison's "Ooby Dooby"? We caught up with Frakes for "First Contact's" 30th anniversary to hear why this "Trek" treasure holds up and warp back to Hollywood’s heyday of the '90s. Resistance is futile! "What’s not to love?" Frakes tells SPACE regarding the film’s lasting popularity. "It was bulletproof. Dean Devlin ["Stargate," "Independence Day"] and I have very similar sensibilities about filmmaking. We like the whole idea of action, adventure, comedy, and in the case of 'First Contact,' a little horror as well. ILM’s John Knoll, the guy who won the Oscar for 'Star Wars,' just happened to be our Special Effects Supervisor." "Star Trek: First Contact" celebrates its 30th birthday on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: Paramount) "First Contact" is filled with memorable moments and indelible performances, some of which certainly stand out for Frakes looking back over the years on the production. science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. My biggest concern isn't necessarily the number of people watching the eclipse, but the logistical chaos it will create. Let's take Mallorca as an example for the 2026 eclipse. Authorities there had a plan for its west coast, the prime viewing region. "They were going to start closing roads from 3 p.m. on the afternoon of the eclipse," said Simon Waldram , who runs astrophotography and landscape photography workshops and who drove his tour group to the intended viewing location at 8 o'clock on the morning of the eclipse. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate . What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image — and many similar images — is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

science.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. science.description: null Update for 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 22: On Sunday afternoon (Nov. 22), the BepiColombo team announced that, while the spacecraft did successfully arrive in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), things didn't go entirely according to plan. "During the manoeuvre, the thruster burn was shorter than planned due to a software issue," the mission team said via X . "The spacecraft is safe & teams at ESOC are working to understand what happened. Updates provided on Monday." For just the second time ever, Mercury has received a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — arrived in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. Before BepiColombo, just one spacecraft had ever circled the solar system's innermost planet: NASA's MESSENGER , which did so from March 2011 to April 2015. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must therefore shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. There was a bit drama involved, however, as confirmation of the maneuver's success didn't come for several hours afterward. "We've heard back from Bepi — the spacecraft is now in contact with the ground and the teams at ESOC [the European Space Operations Centre] are busy assessing the telemetry.
